claims.claim: A commenter recalls a lost WotC developer blog from the 3.5/4e era saying boxed text should never exceed three sentences; the source is gone and WotC did not follow it consistently.
claims.quote: should never be longer than three sentences

claims.claim: The DMs Guild bundle (2018) comprises the IP guide, the adventure design guide, the style guide, and the Realms style guide, originally distributed to organized-play writers.
claims.source: EN World, "DMsGuild: D&D Style-Guides give a unique insight into the game" (2018-11-25)

claims.feature: WotC violates its own tenday rule
claims.claim: EN World readers noted WotC hardcovers still use 'week' despite the guides' tenday rule, reading the guides as newly formalized standards.
claims.source: EN World, "DMsGuild: D&D Style-Guides give a unique insight into the game" (2018-11-25)

claims.claim: The Realms guide's directive that characters should not travel to Sigil was read as WotC reserving Planescape for a future product.
claims.source: EN World, "DMsGuild: D&D Style-Guides give a unique insight into the game" (2018-11-25)
claims.quote: characters should not be traveling there

claims.feature: no public style guide update since 2019
claims.claim: As of 2025-06-13 a DMs Guild creator asked whether the style guide had been updated for the 2024 rules or Chicago 18th; the thread had no reply, confirming the public document is still the 2019 release.
claims.source: D&D Beyond forums, "Is there an update to the D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing document yet?" (2025-06-13)

claims.feature: where the current AL kit lives
claims.claim: The AL resources post (updated 2026-08-12) links the Dungeoncraft Creator Pack of 2023-12-04 on D&D Beyond's CDN while listing the Design Guide as 'coming soon'.
claims.source: D&D Beyond forums, "D&D Adventurers League Resources & Links (Updated 08/12/2026)"

claims.claim: EN World's 2023 report of the Planescape Dungeoncraft update states adventures must use official templates and comply with the D&D Style Guide and DMsGuild Content Guidelines or face removal.
claims.source: EN World, "D&D Adventurers League Unveils New DungeonCraft Document with Planescape In Focus" (2023-11)

claims.claim: WotC's 2020-06-18 statement committed to sensitivity readers on sourcebooks and to reviewing reprints for racially insensitive text.
claims.source: Gizmodo/io9, "Dungeons & Dragons Team Announces New Plans to Address Racism in the Game" (James Whitbrook, 2020-06-18)
claims.quote: That's just not right, and it's not something we believe in.

claims.claim: WotC said it worked with a Romani consultant to revise Curse of Strahd's Vistani text and named Tomb of Annihilation as needing similar updates.
claims.source: Gizmodo/io9, "Dungeons & Dragons Team Announces New Plans to Address Racism in the Game" (2020-06-18)

claims.claim: The statement said recent reprints of Tomb of Annihilation and Curse of Strahd already changed racially insensitive text, and each book would be reviewed at reprint.
claims.source: Wikipedia, "Tomb of Annihilation" (fetched 2026-09-06), quoting the 2020-06-17 WotC statement
claims.quote: we changed text that was racially insensitive

claims.claim: Ray Winninger said only the text of Curse of Strahd was revised; art and tarokka cards were unchanged and the revised text went free to prior D&D Beyond owners.
claims.source: Gizmodo/io9, "D&D's Culturally Sensitive Strahd Revamp Is Here, But It Doesn't Go Far Enough" (Julie Muncy, 2020-07-27)

claims.feature: Strahd Revamped: what the prose fix targeted
claims.claim: The revisions removed the depiction of Vistani as uncivilized heavy drinkers and softened an ableist portrayal, while leaving curse and Evil Eye abilities intact.
WotC's announcement described the revamp as including the latest errata and a revised depiction of the Vistani.
claims.source: Wikipedia, "Curse of Strahd" (fetched 2026-09-06), citing PC Gamer 2020-07
claims.quote: a revised depiction of the Vistani

claims.feature: premise check: a public style guide exists, but not for boxed-text prose
claims.claim: The public WotC D&D Style Guide governs typography, terminology, and grammar only; WotC's only published boxed-text prose rules are the AL adventure-format document's sparing/one-or-two-sentence rule.
claims.source: D&D Style Guide: Writing and Editing, Version 1.08a (2018; 'updated January 2019') together with DC Adventure Format v1.3.docx (Claire Hoffman / Ma'at Crook, 2023-11) in the Dungeoncraft Pack 2023-12-04
